To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
different CT datasets for CBCT registration result in different 6D couch shifts.

3D cone-beam CTs (CBCTs) can be registered to different CT datasets (planning, maximum intensity projection, mid-ventilation, average intensity projection CTs) with different couch shifts (3D setup errors).

the registration of different CT data sets with free breathing cone bean CTs (FB CBCTs) can result in different couch shifts, that manual registrations achieved partly different shifts than automatic registrations, that the use of average intensity projection CTs (AIP) resulted in the smallest differences in shifts and that the differences were statistically correlated with the 3D tumor movement and superior-inferior distance of the lesion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether a registration of the planning CT with the free-breathing cone beam CT is necessary in the case of a lung SBRT.
the registration of different reference CT datasets with free-breathing cone beam CTs in lung SBRT.
the analysis of differences between 3D CBCT and reference CT datasets in the context of lung stereotactic radiation therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of different CT datasets for 3D image registration with CBCTs should be carefully considered.
there is no single optimal CT dataset that can be used as a reference image for registration with 4D CBCTs in lung SBRT.
the choice of the reference CT dataset should be carefully evaluated for each patient and that the registration results should be critically evaluated and if necessary manually corrected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AIP CTs should be used as reference images for image registration with 3DCBCTs in SABR of lung lesions.
for lung SBRT, the AIP CT is the most appropriate reference dataset for image registration with 3DCBCTs.
the use of AIPs for image registration with CBCTs in SBRT of lung tumors is the most appropriate CT data set.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of different CT datasets in image registration can have an impact on the resulting 3D couch shift.
it is important to use the most appropriate reference CT for registration with FB-CBTs.
the registration of CBCTs with different reference CTs should be performed with caution and that the choice of the CT dataset to be used as reference for registration with 4D CBCTs is important.
